name: Antichain Number
definition: Fix a finite ambient domain $X$ and a binary class $\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}$. An **antichain teacher mapping** assigns every $h\in\mathcal H$ a labeled sample $T(h)\subseteq X\times\{0,1\}$ consistent with $h$, such that for distinct $h,g\in\mathcal H$ neither $T(h)\subseteq T(g)$ nor $T(g)\subseteq T(h)$. The **antichain number** $\mathrm{AN}(\mathcal H)$ is the minimum, over such mappings, of $\max_{h\in\mathcal H}|T(h)|$, with value zero for an empty class. Inclusion is inclusion of labeled samples, not just of their coordinate domains. The specified ambient domain is part of the input: constant coordinates may be used and must not be discarded automatically. Subfamily monotonicity keeps this domain fixed; projection and conditioning use their resulting domains.
graph_summary: Smallest maximum size of consistent, pairwise inclusion-incomparable labeled samples. Uses the stated ambient domain, including constant coordinates.
description: A batch-teaching parameter based on antichain mappings of labeled samples.
origin_references: The antichain number is defined and studied in \cite{simon2023map}; its VC upper bound is attributed there to \cite{mansouri2022batch}.

monotonic.proof: Restrict an antichain teacher mapping to a subfamily on the same ambient domain; consistency and sample incomparability are preserved. See the full survey proof.

p_monotonic.proof: The private-coordinate cube has AN one, while its projection onto the original n coordinates has AN growing linearly in n. The database-owned values and the survey proof give the precise construction and bound.

c_monotonic.proof: The nine-concept class {abc00: a,b,c in {0,1}} union {00011} has AN one. Conditioning its fourth coordinate to zero leaves a three-cube with one constant coordinate, of AN two. The survey gives the full teacher map and counting proof. All five coordinates of the original class are active.

doubly_monotonic.proof: Doubly monotonicity requires projection monotonicity, which fails; see Proposition \ref{prop:antichain-monotonicity}.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: The two-cube and both branches of either active coordinate split all have AN one. This violates strict increase over equal branches, independently of the separate conditioning counterexample.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: The equal-branch plus-one identity already fails on the two-cube; see the strict-c counterexample and Proposition \ref{prop:antichain-monotonicity}.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity requires both double monotonicity and strict-c monotonicity, and both fail; see Proposition \ref{prop:antichain-monotonicity}.

symmetric.proof: Complementing every concept and every label in an assigned sample preserves sample consistency, sample cardinality, and inclusion between samples, hence preserves antichain teacher mappings.
